```{python}
from research_site import Study

study = Study()
VERSE = "Verse-level"
PASSAGE = "Passage-level"
```

## Summary

- We fine-tuned two pretrained models, MADLAD and T5Gemma, on the same data as an NLLB baseline for one low-resource language.
- **NLLB scored highest.** MADLAD with verse-level training reached 61.8 passage-level chrF3 against NLLB's 66.7. T5Gemma reached about 44.
- **Training and translating whole passages was worse than single verses** for both alternatives.

## The question

Because oral Bible translation (OBT) projects have passage-level data, can a model like MADLAD or T5Gemma improve on NLLB's translation performance? Unlike NLLB, both MADLAD and T5Gemma have longer context windows that can handle full passages.

## How it was tested

- **Language and data.** Language O (the label used in [combining verses](../2026-11-combining-verses/index.html)), translated from a related language. All models were trained on the whole New Testament except Matthew 11-16, which is the test set. Scores are passage-level chrF3.
- **Models.** NLLB is the baseline. MADLAD and T5Gemma were fine-tuned with silnlp.
- **Verse-level or passage-level.** For a verse-level run, training and inference is done one verse at a time. For a passage-level run, training and inference is done one passage at a time. T5Gemma has a context window was 1,000 tokens.
- **Epochs.** T5Gemma was trained for both 100 and 1,000 epochs at verse level.



## Results

```{python}
study.table(groups=[VERSE, PASSAGE], group_title="Setting", intervals=False, measure_column=False)
```

All results are passage-level chrF3.

- **MADLAD is 4.9 points below NLLB at verse level**, and 17.8 below it at passage level.
- **T5Gemma is about 22 points below NLLB at verse level.** Ten times the epochs added 0.6 points, so training length does not explain the gap.
- **Passage-level training is far worse than verse-level training for MADLAD and T5Gemma.**
- **Cost.** MADLAD did not fit on A100 GPUs or on half of an H100; it needed a full 94 GB H100. T5Gemma ran on half of an H100 (we did not try A100s).

## Limitations

- **One run per setting and no intervals.** Differences within about a point of chrF3 are not established, including 100 against 1,000 epochs.
- **One language and one test set**, six chapters of Matthew.
- **Settings were not tuned per model.** The models may need different hyperparameters than NLLB, so this is a comparison of defaults, not of best possible results.
